title: unified-rollouts: probing weighted canary autorollback workflow optimizations
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Improve probing-weighted canary autorollback workflow to reduce noisy rollbacks by adding quorum-based probing, adaptive thresholds, and enhanced observability. No breaking changes to rollout configs.
description: Context: customers running mixed-traffic canary and shadow experiments saw spurious auto-rollbacks when probing metrics had high variance in early probing windows. This PR introduces a probing-weighted canary autorollback optimization that: 1) uses a quorum of probing samples across users/regions before counting a metric as violating, 2) weights probe contributions by request confidence and latency, 3) smooths early-window metric spikes with an exponential decay guard, and 4) exposes additional telemetry for debugging. Motivation: reduce unnecessary rollbacks and improve stability of progressive rollouts while maintaining safety. Design summary: changes to the autorollback engine add a probing aggregator that collects per-probing-stage samples, computes weighted composites, and only triggers rollbacks when composite metrics exceed configured thresholds and the quorum condition is satisfied. To keep existing behavior, default rollout policies remain unchanged; the new behavior is opt-in via rollout.alpha.probingWeighted flag and rollout.probe.quorum and rollout.probe.weightBy fields. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-5123) attached; - [x] unit tests for aggregator; - [x] integration tests for staged probing scenarios; - [x] e2e canary run in perf-canary lab; - [x] observability dashboards updated. Risks and mitigations: risk of delayed rollback in true regressions mitigated by a configurable minimum-detection window and emergency manual-quarantine API. Migration: operators can flip rollout.alpha.probingWeighted to true in rollout config to enable. Rolling out to production will be gated by canary lab results and a campaign rollout in the Dedicated fleet. Related: builds on previous autorollback work (ENG-4190) and addresses incidents SUP-2321 and postmortem notes from incident-2024-08.
